title: Step 2: Adding Functionality to the Overloaded Operators

blocks.content: Step 2: Adding Functionality to the Overloaded Operators
Now, let's focus our attention on performing the calculations inside the operator() functions. The basic steps for this calculation are:

items: Create a Complex object inside the operator() function to store the result.
Use the respective arithmetic formula to calculate the real and imaginary values.
Return the Complex object that has the result of the calculation.

blocks.content: For the sake of clarity, let's look at a code snippet of the overloaded + operator. This will help you better analyze the other overloaded operators:
Here, we have created the complex_sum object to store the result of the complex addition.
We add the real variable of the calling object (this->real) and the real variable of the argument arg (arg.real) and store it in the real variable of the complex_sum object.
We then repeat the same process for the imag variables of those objects. Finally, we return the complex_sum object.
Now, let's add functionality to all the other overloaded operators.
